svg.text: MONSTER MAHJONG — the self-play game state, animated (194 → 160)
the whole board of 194 irrep tiles, collapsing move-by-move as Conway and Grothendieck merge duplicates.
each merge removes exactly one tile — it slides onto the surviving copy of its 15-bit address and dims. every removal replays the verified transcript (MahjongGameStateSvg.lean).
John Horton Conway, born Liverpool, 26 December 1937.
The Monster M is the largest of the 26 sporadic groups.
1970: the Game of Life — a cellular automaton, Turing-complete.
He rebuilds algebraic geometry on the language of schemes.
196883 is the smallest faithful Monster representation; the +1 is trivial.
From the Leech lattice he builds the Conway groups Co1, Co2, Co3.
EGA and SGA: the relentless rising tide of generality.
He invents the surreal numbers (named later by Knuth).
Topos theory: geometry as a category of sheaves.
Fifteen 'Monster primes' divide |M| — the studs on every tile.
Fields Medal, 1966 (he boycotted the Moscow ceremony).
1979: Conway & Norton state the Monstrous Moonshine conjectures.
The Happy Family: 20 of the sporadics are subquotients of M.
He is a co-author of the ATLAS of Finite Groups.
Each Hauptmodul coefficient is a sum of Monster character degrees.
The 6 pariahs sit outside M: J1, J3, J4, Ru, Ly, O'N.
The Free Will theorem (with Simon Kochen).
'La mer qui monte' — the rising sea dissolves the problem.
Frenkel–Lepowsky–Meurman build the Monster vertex algebra V♮.
1985: the ATLAS of Finite Groups (Conway, Curtis, Norton, Parker, Wilson).
1991: he withdraws to the Pyrenees; Récoltes et Semailles.
M has 194 conjugacy classes — hence 194 irreducible characters.
prime faces — a tile's lit studs are the Monster primes dividing its dimension (its 15-bit content-address):
“Do not attack the object. Raise the water until only its essential structure remains.”
— the rising sea, after Alexander Grothendieck · the self-play is verified in MahjongGameService.lean; this animation replays it.
